title: Fairview at Young Vic - Review (with spoilers)
transcript: I'm Paul seven Louis this is the Young Vic and I'm here to review Fairview what are you looking at says the wife to the husband right at the beginning of the play but that really is the question what are you looking at we start out with what seemed like a pastiche of a u.s. TV sitcom featuring an african-american family funny but not that special then we come to act 2 and everything turns upside down from here on in we are in no doubt that this is about race about the white gays about racial and other stereotypes about what it means to be black not that Jackie's syphilis drury presents a simple lecture about racist stereotypes and cultural appropriation fairview is subtle it has many layers all presented with comedy and a unique theatricality and directed with flair Viner Diala teeth i won't say too much in this one-minute review because if you're going to see Fairview and I think you should the surprises are part of the experience I'll explore what happens in detail with spoilers in my longer review which comes after this suffice to say that what happens in the course of the play when white people intervene will have you questioning what happened in the first act and who these people are because you'll see the drama rewrite itself through the next two acts and an extraordinary coda I give Fairview four stars Fairview is much more than the play it's a theatrical experience and when it seems we're looking at a well-off african-american family about to enjoy dinner party but there's something not quite right is it a drama set around a dinner party well they've been plenty of them over the years with their bickering and jealousy and secrets but this seems more like a u.s. sitcom the set designed by Tom Scott is so wonderfully bright and clean the characters are black yes which in our world of middle-class theatres is unusual so we may anticipate that race is going to figure but these are middle class people shut your eyes and the characters could be any color the wife Beverly played by Nicola Hughes with a perfect mix of bossiness insecurities and affection the playful husband Dayton played by Russian stone Nana a gay Anthony squeezes all the comedy she can from the fashion-conscious fatty sister jasmine and Donna banner is the sensitive rebellious daughter Keisha plus off stage the unreliable brother hoping for a partnership in his firm the daughter's friend the mother who won't come downstairs or to be honest amusing but entirely predictable there are on moments the radio of malfunctioning briefly a tendency to break into dance the daughter appearing in a spotlight to express her discomfort with the situation then in act two first spoiler alert we see the same scene but this time acted out silently while the radio look maybe the radio provides the commentary from four white people who are they they could be the creators of the characters were seeing or they could simply be ciphers for the white games anyway they digress into a long discussion about what race they would like to be each time coming up with these stereotypical views of those races ending with black where they conclude that the kind of middle-class black people that we are viewing a boring because it's poor black people that are interesting the rappers that allow manners the voice who would like to be black remembers fondly her black mane this does go on a bit but then there's a wonderful moment when the characters on stage previously unsynchronized segue into apparently mouthing what the voices are saying even though we can remember that this wasn't the dialogue from the first act so the offstage and onstage characters kind of come together in a prelude to the third act because if that wasn't enough in the third act and here's another spoiler we'd pick up the story of the family and it's not long before the white characters that we heard talking decide to come on to the stage to spice up this middle-class family with more interesting black characters that they play so the missing brother appears as a rapper although his sister's still asking how the partnership is going the mother appears twice once as the remembered black maid with a history that Beverly contradicts the white people question and provoke the black people and the black people object to being told what they are it all ends in an amazing food fight then in a final coup that final spoiler the daughter invites those in the audience identifying us white to come up on stage and see what it feels like to be in the spotlight not to be normal not to be in the majority in the audience but to be focused upon expected to be a certain way simply because of the color of your skin the actors leave the stage and many of the audience climb onto the stage including me it was an interesting experience the lights are blinding you can't see the audience or what's left of it you go from being an anonymous member of that audience to being the focus of attention now I tend to think that theatre sparkly about letting you into other people's lives or letting us see ourselves in different ways but this really took it from an intellectual exercise to a physical one I think I need to say that this is an American play and I think that's the reason why I didn't feel as powerful to me as much of a punch in the guts as it clearly did too many Americans when it was first performed in the US I think the Americans have quite a strong idea of what black culture is whereas I think we would find it hard to stereotype black British culture although some of us might have prejudices regarding black people as I said before Jackie simplist Rory doesn't present a lecture about racist stereotyping except right at the end if he did I might be saying that she wasn't telling as much we didn't already know instead she starts with a middle-class family and their back knowledge is that education and money are Levellers she subtly shows them being aware of what's expected them but it is subtle it manifests in what you might call watered-down stereotypes Chaucer presents the white people as stereotypes the camp gay man springs to mind which suggests that fair view is not only about race I took from the evening a strong plea to take people as you find them with a fair view rather than imposing preconceptions or prejudices well that's what I carried away but this is such a good play that I think people depending on their backgrounds and prejudices will have come away with many different reactions fair view deserves to be seen and it deserves four stars from me I hope you found this review interesting and helpful if you did please subscribe to my youtube channel one minute theater reviews thank you for watching you
